engagement_title: Marrow and Vane autumn exhibition: rebuild the printer's spring wall label into a live run for forty one works, bring two interns' photography to one record standard, recover the door mark off the brass plate, and hand the checklist back editable
vertical: Arts and culture, a mid career commercial gallery in Philadelphia hanging a nine artist autumn exhibition across three rooms for collectors and institutional curators
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the posted freelance commission this concept sits on: a gallery job asking for printed exhibition wall labels and an accompanying exhibition checklist produced from a works list and a folder of artwork images, one label per hung piece carrying title, artist, medium, dimensions and year, all consistent across the show, with the previous season's printed piece supplied as the look to keep. The real posting names its gallery, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house Marrow and Vane. The ledger verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept and its collateral are right, but the original sat almost entirely on one surface (drop the rows into a template and merge). CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because a bare press PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a checklist with real tables and real type can be authored into a native editable Express document, and a mark can be recovered at ink level off a photograph of the brass fascia. So this is the gallery's actual job: the printer's spring artwork becomes a live run, the interns' photography becomes a record set, and the checklist the desk updates next week is genuinely editable.
client_one_liner: We hang forty one works on the eighteenth, we have no InDesign file for the labels, only the PDF the printer used in spring, and our two interns photographed the works over two days in two different places.
client_brief:
Marrow and Vane, autumn exhibition

We are a commercial gallery in Philadelphia. On the eighteenth we hang forty one works by nine artists across three rooms, and the printer needs the wall labels a week before that.

What we need. One label per hung work: title, artist, year, medium, dimensions, the credit line where there is one, and our accession number small at the foot. They print one to a page on a single card stock, guillotined and mounted by our installers. We do not have a layout file. What we have is the PDF the printer used for the spring show, which is the look we want kept exactly, because the rooms are hung the same way and the labels should not look like a new decision. We also want the labels back split by room in hang order, so the installers are not sorting a stack of forty one.

We need the checklist too, the folded document that sits on the desk and goes out with the press list. Same works, in hang order, in three room sections, with a small reference picture of each work. It has to be something we can update ourselves the week after, when two works sell and one comes off the wall.

The pictures. Our two interns photographed the works, some in the storeroom and some already hung, over two days. They are not consistent and a few are behind glass. On the checklist they should read as one set of records, not as photographs of a gallery.

Our mark exists as an etched brass plate by the door, and a photograph of it. We would like it on the checklist properly, rather than as a picture of brass.

The works run from six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars and the room is collectors and two institutional curators. The labels should be quiet. Tell us what you did, and anything you could not do.
price_band_and_audience: Works at six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars, audience collectors and two institutional curators, plus a press list. The band is load-bearing: at this level the label is austere and generously spaced, a small quiet type size sitting high on a large card with a lot of unprinted stock under it, no rules, no colour, no logo on the label at all, because typographic restraint is how the institution signals that the work carries the room. Drop the same show to a two hundred dollar community group show and the correct label is warmer and denser: bigger type, the gallery mark on every card, a price line, a QR to the artist's page, all of which would read here as a market stall. Push the other way into a museum's editorial house style with a wall text paragraph per work and the labels start competing with the art and misrepresent a selling show as a survey. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every field maps correctly. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Arts and culture: a mid-career commercial gallery mounting selling exhibitions of contemporary work for collectors and institutional curators.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A commercial gallery in Philadelphia hanging across three rooms, run by a director with a small registrar and installation team.
brand_identity.about: Marrow and Vane is a Philadelphia gallery that mounts selling shows for collectors and curators. The house look is austere and generously spaced: the label and the checklist stay quiet so the work carries the room. Their autumn exhibition hangs forty one works by nine artists across three rooms.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors and institutional curators, plus a press list. Readers who scan a medium line for provenance and expect the gallery to signal seriousness through restraint rather than through decoration.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Works from six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars. At this level the label is small, quiet type high on a large card with unprinted stock beneath, no rules, no colour, no logo on the card. It must read as a selling show, not a community group show and not a museum survey.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained institutional system: a quiet text face at a small size for the title, artist, medium, dimensions and accession, with the botanical restraint of a gallery hand. No display drama; the measure and the white space do the work. The checklist and the labels read as one house.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, precise, factual. The gallery states rather than sells. Example line the brand would write: 'Nine artists. Three rooms. Eighteen September through the second of November.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no layout file for the labels; only the printer's spring press PDF survives as the look to keep. The gallery mark exists as an etched brass plate beside the door and a single photograph of it, and has to be recovered as real artwork before it can sit on the checklist.
brand_identity.values: Restraint as respect for the work: the label serves the art and the record is accurate to the last accession number. The institution shows its seriousness by staying quiet.

assets_supplied.name: mv_spring_labels_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The single page press PDF the gallery's printer used for the spring show's wall label, one label per page, real embedded font subsets, produced from the printer's own layout file.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the file that went to press in spring. Keep the look exactly, the rooms are hung the same way."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as four separated blocks (title, artist line, medium and dimensions, accession) but the converted template's frame granularity is nothing like that, and the credit line is its own run inside a continuous story. The mapping readout omits that run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator still returns VALID with no warnings.

assets_supplied.name: mv_autumn_works.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Forty one rows, one per hung work: catalogue number, artist, title, year, medium, dimensions, credit line, accession number, room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The works list as the registrar keeps it. The medium lines are the artists' own wording and cannot be edited without asking them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three medium lines run far longer than anything in the spring show (one reads oil, wax and rabbit skin glue on linen mounted on aluminium, in two parts) and two dimensions carry a two part measurement. In a fixed label frame at true trim the text does not spill and no overset is reported anywhere: it simply stops rendering, and the page count still equals the row count. Two rows carry a credit line and thirty nine are empty, and one year is a range rather than a single year.

assets_supplied.name: mv_works_photography/ (44 files)
assets_supplied.kind: Reference photography of the works shot by two interns over two days, some in the storeroom against a grey wall and some already hung under gallery track lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The interns shot everything. They are not consistent and a few are behind glass."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Forty four files do not mean forty four works: two files are the same painting shot twice (a full view and a detail) and one hung work has no photograph at all, which no filename or column reveals. Three works are glazed and carry the track lights in the varnish, so a global lift takes the reflection with it. The files are named by accession number while the works list keys by catalogue number under a different scheme.

assets_supplied.name: mv_brass_plate.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the etched brass fascia plate beside the gallery door, the mark cut into brushed brass: a compound lockup of two words joined by an ampersand, sitting under a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark by the door. We would like it on the checklist properly rather than as a picture of brass."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The etched ink and the brushed ground run close in value across the lit half of the plate, and the ampersand and the hairline rule are the thinnest parts of the lockup. A trace that looks clean and complete at full canvas closes its counters at the size the checklist actually reproduces the mark, on the warm grey ground the checklist uses, which is a different ground and a different size from the one it was judged on.

assets_supplied.name: mv_hang_order.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text, the installer's hang order by room from the walkthrough.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The order the works go up in, room by room."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two works appear in two rooms because they were moved during the walkthrough and nobody struck the first entry, and the last two positions in the third room are recorded as to be confirmed.

assets_supplied.name: mv_desk_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the gallery director: the show title, dates, the three room names, the press contact line and the credit wording convention.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The house wording. Credits are set exactly as written."

acceptance_bar: The wall label run is one press PDF with one work per page and the page count equal to the row count, and every field the spring card carries is present on every page, including the credit line on the two works that have one.
No label is short of its own record. A medium line, a dimension or a credit that stops before its last word fails the run even though the page count is right and every response reported success.

The forty one labels are one typographic system: one type size per role across every card, one measure, one position on the card. A single label rescued by being set smaller than its neighbours fails.
The label artwork is the spring card, not a new design. Type, position, measure and card size are carried over rather than reinterpreted.

The installers get the run split by room in hang order as named single record files, with the room and the position in the name, and the identity of each file is guaranteed rather than inferred from the order links came back in.
Every reference picture on the checklist is of the work it is captioned as, every hung work has one, and no picture stands in for two works.

The reference set reads as records rather than as photographs of a gallery: one white point, one black point, the work square in the frame and cropped to its own edge, with the wall, the floor and the frame's shadow out.

The recovered mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of brass: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as our mark at the size it actually prints on the checklist, on the checklist's own ground.

The checklist is one editable document with the three rooms as real sections and the works as a real table we can retype, not a picture of a list, and it opens with the type still in the licensed faces.

The note records what was applied per photograph, the type system by role with the family and the real weight used, the reconciliation between the photography folder and the works list, and everything the gallery asked for that could not be produced.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, template archaeology and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (both as a readout and as a validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange and additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution, pageRange)
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole label run. It reverse engineers the printer's spring press PDF into a live merge template with no native file supplied, which means reading what the conversion actually exposes rather than what the printed card implies, computing every text offset against the document's true story rather than the readout, verifying placeholders by round tripping the document rather than trusting a success message, merging forty one records one to a page, and rendering the per room subsets in hang order with identity guaranteed rather than inferred.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Two separate jobs. It brings forty one reference photographs shot in two places on two days to one record standard, cropping each work to its own edge from an explicit selection rather than trusting a subject focused crop against a grey wall, and confining corrections on the glazed works so a global lift does not carry the track lights with it. Then it recovers the door mark at ink level off a photograph of brushed brass and performs the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The checklist as a native editable document the desk updates the week after the opening, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout with real tables. Every reference picture must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector at its real printed size, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because forty one inlined pictures pass the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The checklist type system and the specification of the label faces in the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet and institutional rather than editorial or decorative at a six thousand to eighty five thousand dollar band. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

The curator and registrar review surface. The normalised record set is persisted to a shareable board in hang order so the director signs off which frame represents each work before any of them are bound into the checklist, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and re sent only for the entries the response names as failed. Adobe Stock is deliberately not used anywhere in this engagement, because a licensed photograph has no place in a record of a specific artwork.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The labels are a genuine variable data run at one record per page and belong on the merge surface; the checklist is a small number of composed pages with three sections and a table, which the merge surface cannot lay out at all and which the gallery must edit next week. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the press PDF, the works list, the hang order, the desk note, the brass plate photograph and every reference frame through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest has to be keyed by catalogue number rather than by filename, because the filenames are keyed to a different scheme than the list.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by catalogue number.

trajectory.action: Read the works list against the photography folder and the hang order, and settle how many works there are, how many have a picture, and what the hang order actually says.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts forty one works and hands over forty four files and an order list. The files and the list are the only things that can settle whether that is forty one pictures of forty one works, and counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A reconciliation table: work to picture to room to hang position, with the gaps, the duplicates and the two contested positions named rather than guessed.

trajectory.action: Convert the spring press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and look at the real frame inventory: how many text frames, what bounds, what applied faces and sizes, what object styles, what the story actually contains.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what its file exposes as separately addressable are different questions, and only the exported structure answers the second one. Promising a per field frame mapping before looking is a promise about somebody else's file.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with counts, bounds, applied typography and the document's true story text.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story by concatenating the document's own content runs, and compute every text offset from that string rather than from the readout the mapping tool returns.
trajectory.judgement: The readout is a convenience view of a story, not the story. Any offset computed against a convenience view is an offset into a string the document does not contain.
trajectory.produces: The true story text per frame and an offset table computed against it.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the true offsets, run it back through the validator, then prepare the merge template so the spring card carries live placeholders for every field the label needs.
trajectory.judgement: Which action suits each field is a real choice on a template that has no tokens in it, and the credit line that only two works carry cannot be mapped the same way as a field every work has.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template with placeholders and a datasource attached.

trajectory.action: Round trip the prepared template back out to its interchange form and search its stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to write.
trajectory.judgement: The preparation step reports success while silently dropping mappings, so the only evidence that a field landed is the field being findable in the document afterwards. This is the difference between a report and a verification.
trajectory.produces: A per field present or absent verdict on the prepared template.

trajectory.action: Preview the reference frames and bring them to one record standard: level what is off, one white point and one black point across storeroom and gallery light, each work cropped to its own edge from an explicit selection of the work rather than a subject focused crop against a grey wall, with confined corrections on the three glazed works.
trajectory.judgement: A record is not a photograph: the wall, the floor and the frame shadow are not part of the work. On a glazed painting a whole frame lift raises the reflection with the image, so the correction has to be confined by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the object it hangs on.
trajectory.produces: Forty normalised records at source scale with a per frame parameter log and the missing work named.

trajectory.action: Create the review board, add the normalised records in hang order within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, and put the reconciliation in front of the director.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, not an error. The board exists so the director resolves the duplicate work, the missing photograph and the two contested hang positions before anything is bound into a document.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and a signed off reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Build the merge data from the works list, with the picture column carried in the form the merge binds and the per work files named to match, then merge all forty one records to a press document, one work per page.
trajectory.judgement: A merge that places one static picture on every record is the default failure here, and the column has to be shaped so each record pulls its own frame.
trajectory.produces: A merged press document carrying all forty one records.

trajectory.action: Render the run at trim at print resolution and read the pages, not the response.
trajectory.judgement: The response reports pages, not sentences. Reading the pages is the only channel that reports what a specific string did inside a specific frame at a specific size.
trajectory.produces: A rendered label run inspected page by page against the works list.

trajectory.action: Produce the per room subsets in hang order as named single record files, with identity guaranteed by the route rather than assumed from the order the links came back in.
trajectory.judgement: Multi record raster output comes back in an order its own labels contradict, so the safe routes are the ones where identity is structural: separate files off the merged document, or one record per call.
trajectory.produces: Named single record files per room in hang order for the installers.

trajectory.action: Recover the door mark off the brass plate: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties rather than the plate it is cut into, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the etched line and not the brushed brass, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable for a document printed in one ink.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the checklist.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a quiet institutional register and against the faces the spring label already uses, so the checklist and the labels read as one house rather than two jobs. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author the checklist as one self contained document: three room sections in hang order, the works as a real table, each reference picture carried as embedded image data, the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper at the size it actually prints, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and the design decision is how much unprinted ground the band takes and how small the mark can sit and still be the mark.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the whole checklist, retained as the durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first page, and parse the returned per page markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first page. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable checklist document, an inspected first page, and a per page markup audit for the remainder.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per photograph and why, the type system by role with family, foundry and the real numeric weight, the reconciliation between the folder and the list, the identity route used for the per room files, and everything asked for that could not be produced.
trajectory.judgement: The gallery asked for a press ready run, and a converted template carries no bleed and cannot be given any, so that has to be said plainly rather than quietly delivered without it. The note has to be specific enough that next season's freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A written handover naming the limits as clearly as the results.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping claimed to write are actually in the prepared template. The spring card presents as four separated blocks, but what the conversion exposes is a continuous story in which the credit line is its own run, and the mapping readout omits that run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed. Every offset computed past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, and the preparation step returns a completed successfully message, and only some of the fields are present in the document afterwards. Which fields survived is visible in no response at all, only in the prepared template's own stories.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and care does not either, because the readout looks correct and the validator confirms it; the mitigation (rebuild the story from the document's own runs and recompute every offset against that) is only obviously worth its cost once the round trip has shown fields missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that there is no layout file and the spring PDF is the look to keep. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different derivation of the offsets from a different source string, and on this template the credit line may have to be mapped by a different action entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild each frame's true story from the document's content runs, recompute the whole offset table against it, remap the credit line by an action that suits a field only two of forty one records carry, prepare the template again and round trip it again before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty one wall labels that go to press missing the credit line and the accession foot, with the page count correct, every response reporting success, and the omission first visible on the wall on opening night.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the three long medium lines and the two part dimensions actually do inside a fixed label frame at true trim. They do not spill and they do not report an overset anywhere in the merge response: the text simply stops rendering at the frame's bottom, mid phrase, and the merged document still has one page per record and the page count still equals the row count. Where a proportional string of that length breaks, inside that measure at that point size, is not computable from the frame bounds and the typography the template reports, and the rendered page is the only channel that shows it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The defensible order is exactly this one, prepare then merge then render then read, and there is no capacity readout anywhere in the chain and no overset flag in a merged output. (b) Nothing states it: the client says the medium lines are the artists' own wording and cannot be edited without asking, which is a permissions statement about the copy, not a warning that a frame will silently truncate it. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a set wide decision rather than a repeat: the run is one typographic system, so a single label cannot be rescued by being set smaller, and the choice is between a smaller size across all forty one, a wider measure on every card that changes the spring look the client asked to keep exactly, an abbreviation convention applied consistently and cleared with the registrar, or going back to the gallery on three specific works.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Decide the treatment for the whole run rather than the three offending records, change the template or the copy convention accordingly, prepare again if the frame changed, merge all forty one again, render at trim again and read every page rather than the three that were known to be long.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three works hung with labels that stop mid phrase, on a selling show where the medium line is the collector's provenance, with the page count, the field mapping and every tool response all reporting a clean run.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size the checklist actually reproduces it, on the ground the checklist actually uses. The trace is judged at full canvas against the plate, where it is clean, complete and correct: the ampersand's counters open, the hairline rule present. Placed at its real size on the checklist's warm grey ground, and rendered by the importer rather than by a browser, the thinnest parts are where the etched line and the brushed brass ran closest in value, and the counters can close into solid shapes while the rule thins to nothing. Nothing in the trace, the markup or the export response reports it. The rendered page is the only place it exists, and the rendition only returns the first page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the mark cannot be judged at its reproduction size before there is a page that reproduces it at that size, and no tool in the connector reports stroke weight, counter area or contrast against a ground. (b) Nothing states it: the client asks only for the mark placed properly rather than as a picture of brass, which is a request about medium, not a warning about size. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different asset produced by a different route, either a re trace from a selection made on the unlit half of the plate where ink and ground separate, or a colour accurate plate rather than the two colour trace, or a decision to reproduce the mark larger and re compose the checklist masthead around it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re derive the mark by a different selection and polarity, or accept a larger reproduction size and re author the masthead around it, re inject the viewBox and strip the ground path again, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first page alone.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A checklist going out with the press list carrying a gallery mark that has filled in and lost its rule, which is the one element on the document that is the institution rather than the exhibition.

deliverables.name: Autumn wall label run, press PDF plus per room installer files
deliverables.spec: One press PDF of forty one wall labels, one work per page in works list order, built from the printer's own spring artwork rather than a new design, every field present including the credit line on the two works that carry one and the accession number at the foot, and no record truncated at trim. Delivered alongside the same run split by room in hang order as named single record files, with identity guaranteed by the route used rather than inferred from response order. Rendered at print resolution at trim, with the absence of bleed named explicitly in the handover.

deliverables.name: Marrow and Vane autumn record set
deliverables.spec: Forty normalised artwork records brought to one standard across storeroom and gallery lighting: one white point, one black point, each work square and cropped to its own edge with the wall, the floor and the frame shadow out, the three glazed works corrected without lifting their reflections, none enlarged beyond its source frame. Delivered with a per frame parameter log, the folder to works list reconciliation, and the one work with no photograph named rather than substituted.

deliverables.name: Recovered Marrow and Vane mark
deliverables.spec: The door plate lockup recovered from a photograph of etched brass as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the ampersand's counters open and the hairline rule intact at the size the checklist actually prints it and on the checklist's own ground rather than at full canvas.

deliverables.name: Autumn exhibition checklist as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the checklist in three room sections in hang order, the works as a real table the gallery can retype rather than a picture of a list, each work's reference record carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, live text in one licensed type system, and the mark as real vector shapes. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half: the desk edits the document the week after the opening and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Verification note and curator review board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied per photograph and why, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the folder to works list reconciliation, the route used to guarantee per room file identity, and everything the gallery asked for that could not be produced with the reason. Paired with the persistent shareable review board carrying the normalised records in hang order with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The wall label press PDF has exactly one page per row of the works list, in works list order.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the PDF page count and compare it against the row count of the delivered merge data, then read the identifying field on each page against the corresponding row.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field the label carries is present as a live placeholder in the prepared template, including the credit line and the accession number.
verifiers_auto.how: Round trip the prepared template to its interchange form and search its stories for each expected placeholder token.

verifiers_auto.text: Each record's label carries its own reference binding rather than one static picture repeated across the run.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the picture reference resolved on each merged page against the per work column in the delivered merge data.

verifiers_auto.text: The per room installer files are single record files whose named room and position match the signed off hang order.
verifiers_auto.how: Open each named file, read its identifying field, and check the name against the reconciliation table.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered record image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered record against its source per the manifest, and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The checklist exported with its declared page count, the works arrived as a real table, and no reference picture resolved to the importer's placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and per page markup in the export response, count table cell structures, and search the markup for placeholder image data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported checklist carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The review board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the board id and the added entity and failed item arrays from the board responses.

verifiers_human.text: No label stops before its last word. Every medium line, dimension and credit reads complete on the card at trim.
verifiers_human.how: Read all forty one rendered pages at trim against the works list, with particular attention to the longest medium lines and the two part dimensions.

verifiers_human.text: The forty one labels read as one typographic system and as the same card the printer produced in spring.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the rendered pages beside the supplied spring press PDF and judge size per role, measure, position on the card and card size as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The record set reads as records rather than as photographs of a gallery, and the glazed works do not carry the track lights.
verifiers_human.how: View the forty records in a grid at record scale and judge white point, black point, crop logic and reflections as a set.

verifiers_human.text: Every reference picture on the checklist is of the work it is captioned as, every hung work has one, and none stands in for two.
verifiers_human.how: Read the checklist against the works list and the signed off reconciliation.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the gallery's mark at the size the checklist prints it, with open counters and its rule intact, on the checklist's own ground.
verifiers_human.how: View the exported checklist at reproduction size rather than at full canvas, and against the brass plate photograph.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a six thousand to eighty five thousand dollar selling show, quiet and generously spaced, rather than as a community show or as a museum survey.
verifiers_human.how: Judge type size, density, unprinted ground and the presence or absence of gallery branding on the label against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the gallery something it did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered and why.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the reconciliation, the identity route and every limitation are named.

decision_gates: Which deliverable belongs on the merge surface and which needs an authored fixed canvas document, given that a record per page run and a three section checklist are not the same shape of problem.
What the converted spring template actually exposes as addressable, and therefore whether fields can be mapped per frame or must be placed inside one continuous story.
Which string the offsets are computed against: the readout the mapping tool returns, or the document's own reconstructed story.
How to map a credit line that only two of forty one records carry, without leaving a hole on the other thirty nine.
Whether forty four files for forty one works is forty one works photographed, and how to say so when it is not.
Crop logic for a record: what counts as the work and what is the wall, the floor and the frame shadow, applied identically across storeroom and gallery light.
Whether to correct the three glazed works globally or to confine the correction, and how to word a selection so it takes the varnish reflection and not the painting.

What to do when a medium line does not fit: a smaller size across all forty one, a wider measure that changes the spring look, an abbreviation convention cleared with the registrar, or a conversation about three specific works.
Which route guarantees per room file identity, given that response order is not evidence of record order.
Selection wording on the brass plate: naming the plate takes the brass, naming the etched line's own visual properties takes the mark, and the lit half of the plate is not where the two separate.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet institutional register and against the faces the spring label already uses.
How small the mark can sit on the checklist and still be the mark, judged on the checklist's ground at its printed size rather than at full canvas.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a gallery label. IDENTITY: these are forty one specific works with specific artists, specific media in the artists' own wording, specific accession numbers and two specific credit lines, and the label is the printer's existing spring artwork that the client asked to keep exactly, not a restyled interpretation of it; a regenerated label is a different gallery's label with invented provenance on it. SPEC: the run is one press PDF with one work per page and a page count equal to the row count, rendered at print resolution at trim, plus per room single record files in hang order whose identity is guaranteed, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the checklist is defined by being editable, because two works sell and one comes off the wall the week after the opening and the desk updates it themselves. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this field actually land in the template, did this medium line stop rendering at the frame's bottom, does this traced mark still have its counters at the size it prints.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, including building a live merge template from a bare press PDF with no native file supplied, one record per page confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per row image binding via an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles confirmed visually, per record separate files and a recordRange loop both verified in correct order, and true 300 DPI raster via document_render_layout. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: the mapping readout is verified LOSSY (it dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, every later offset was short by exactly 17, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, prepare reported completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed); frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the author's control and capable of collapsing to a single frame; and the label truncation gate rests on there being no overset report anywhere in the merge chain, with the rendered page at trim the only channel. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area and vectorize are verified headless; the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are live findings and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: real tables with per cell backgrounds, strokes and text are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup; transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: boards_create_new_board and boards_add_items_to_board persist genuinely, with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED AND NAMED: no bleed is claimed (a PDF derived template carries none and cannot be given any, which the handover must state), no pdfPreset, no variable QR, no resolution parameter trusted on merge output, no multi record per page, no per record raster named from response order, no upscaling, no OCR, no image to PDF, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no Stock, no batch above 20.
